GPS turns travel time into distance. In one microsecond, a radio signal travels about 300 metres. A fast phone clock adds the same extra distance to every reading. A fourth well-placed satellite gives the receiver another measurement to solve for that shared error.

The measurements

Measured travel time × speed of light = pseudorange, the distance the phone’s clock suggests.

Back to receiver
SignalTrue distanceMeasured timePseudorangeFit residual
Show the receiver’s calculations

Each signal gives pseudorange = distance to satellite + clock bias. The receiver begins at the survey origin with zero clock bias. It predicts the ranges, finds the change that best reduces the squared residuals, then repeats. The table shows the guesses after each update.

UpdateEastNorthUpClock error

Fit residual = measured range minus predicted range. Horizontal dilution of precision (HDOP) is the horizontal uncertainty per metre of independent range noise in this model.

What this model simplifies

One simulated instant, with fixed satellite positions at GPS orbital altitude and a phone that stays in the same place. The receiver uses straight-line distances in three dimensions. The ground view is an invented local map. The clock offset is shared across measurements and the echo adds extra path to one signal. The simulation omits atmospheric delays, satellite-clock corrections and Earth rotation during signal flight.
